svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: The same participant-safe task and benchmark-owned concurrent initial workstreams enter independent Linear and Async routes. A, B and C illustrate independent subagents, not a required count or model pool. Private event rules define affected and preserved work across eight themes. Linear waits for every terminal child state before showing one stable batch. Async shares a qualitative time axis. Main work overlaps all children and continues after A completes. Scenario control holds that real result until a case-dependent condition permits release. In this example, the evaluator observes the main reaching Draft ready, a provisional-artifact checkpoint. The dashed observation line is not a command from main and does not expose private event rules. The matching Event rules lock badge refers to the private case contract above; it is not a continuous data edge. Other cases can use different conditions; the illustrated artifact-trigger policy has bounded waiting and a fallback. The solid result path runs through Hold, Trigger and Release and then reaches actual presentation in a launched main-model request. Public submission validation and adapter queueing remain operational details, separate from hidden scoring. The Async interrupt changes subsequent main work without preempting its in-flight API request. Main responds, continues and selectively cancels B while C retains its original task and keeps working. No in-place task mutation or automatic replacement child is implied, and cancellation is not mandatory for all events. Time is unitless, unmeasured and not to scale; internal control-card positions are a mechanism flow, not time measurements. Run records cover the whole execution, actions, actual presentation and event-boundary artifact digests. BTS arrows denote eventual whole-run final states. Independent DRS uses half process and half event outcome without strict single-response-window causal attribution. Each metric aggregates through repetitions and tasks to equal-weight theme means with coverage reported separately.
